- Wording a scholar should check first: 26:177 (named without the word brother), 26:185 (bewitched), 26:189 (the day of the shadow), 15:79 (the dual pronoun), 38:13 (factions).
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the claim that the Companions of the Thicket and the people of Madyan are one people sent the same messenger; the draft keeps them apart.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The call to the Companions of the Thicket  (`#the-call-to-the-thicket`)

Cited ayat: 26:176-184

> **26:176** كَذَّبَ أَصْحَٰبُ لْـَٔيْكَةِ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
>
> **26:177** إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ شُعَيْبٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
>
> **26:178** إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ
>
> **26:179** فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
>
> **26:180** وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
>
> **26:181** أَوْفُوا۟ ٱلْكَيْلَ وَلَا تَكُونُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلْمُخْسِرِينَ
>
> **26:182** وَزِنُوا۟ بِٱلْقِسْطَاسِ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمِ
>
> **26:183** وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا۟ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشْيَآءَهُمْ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ
>
> **26:184** وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُمْ وَٱلْجِبِلَّةَ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (26:176): The Quran says that the Companions of the Thicket denied the messengers.

**c2** (26:177): Shu'ayb said to them: will you not fear God.

**c3** (26:178-179): Shu'ayb told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him.

**c4** (26:180): Shu'ayb told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds.

**c5** (26:181-182): Shu'ayb told them to give full measure, not to be among those who cause loss, and to weigh with the straight balance.

**c6** (26:183): Shu'ayb told them not to diminish people's things and not to spread corruption in the land.

**c7** (26:184): Shu'ayb told them to fear Him who created them and the earlier creations.

### One-minute summary

The Companions of the Thicket denied the messengers, and Shu'ayb called them to fear God and to obey him [c1][c2][c3]. He told them to give full measure, to weigh with the straight balance and not to spread corruption [c5][c6].

### Complete story

The Quran says that the Companions of the Thicket denied the messengers [c1]. Shu'ayb said to them: will you not fear God [c2]. Shu'ayb told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him [c3]. Shu'ayb told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds [c4]. Shu'ayb told them to give full measure, not to be among those who cause loss, and to weigh with the straight balance [c5]. Shu'ayb told them not to diminish people's things and not to spread corruption in the land [c6]. Shu'ayb told them to fear Him who created them and the earlier creations [c7].

### Deep study

- The Quran says that the Companions of the Thicket denied the messengers (26:176) [c1].
- Shu'ayb said to them: will you not fear God (26:177) [c2].
- Shu'ayb told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him (26:178-179) [c3].
- Shu'ayb told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds (26:180) [c4].
- Shu'ayb told them to give full measure, not to be among those who cause loss, and to weigh with the straight balance (26:181-182) [c5].
- Shu'ayb told them not to diminish people's things and not to spread corruption in the land (26:183) [c6].
- Shu'ayb told them to fear Him who created them and the earlier creations (26:184) [c7].

### Kids mode

Shu'ayb spoke to the Companions of the Thicket [c2]. He told them to fear God [c3]. He told them to give full measure and not to take away from people what belonged to them [c5][c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The call joins fear of God with fairness in measure and weight [c3][c5]. One reading is that honest dealing appears here as part of what the messenger asks, together with a refusal of any wage [c4][c5].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the ayat of 26:177 name Shu'ayb but do not call him their brother, unlike other ayat that call a messenger their brother; the draft does not say whether this people is the same as another people.
- Not established: what the Thicket was, where it was, or how many Companions there were.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any identification of the Thicket with a place, and any link to Madyan; none is used here.

## 2. The day of the shadow  (`#the-day-of-the-shadow`)

Cited ayat: 15:78-79, 26:177, 26:185-190, 38:13

> **15:78** وَإِن كَانَ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلْأَيْكَةِ لَظَٰلِمِينَ
>
> **15:79** فَٱنتَقَمْنَا مِنْهُمْ وَإِنَّهُمَا لَبِإِمَامٍ مُّبِينٍ

> **26:177** إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ شُعَيْبٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ

> **26:185** قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسَحَّرِينَ
>
> **26:186** وَمَآ أَنتَ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُنَا وَإِن نَّظُنُّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
>
> **26:187** فَأَسْقِطْ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفًا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
>
> **26:188** قَالَ رَبِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
>
> **26:189** فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَهُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمِ ٱلظُّلَّةِ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
>
> **26:190** إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ

> **38:13** وَثَمُودُ وَقَوْمُ لُوطٍ وَأَصْحَٰبُ لْـَٔيْكَةِ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلْأَحْزَابُ

### Claims

**c1** (26:177, 26:185-186): They told Shu'ayb that he was one of the bewitched, a human like them, and that they thought him one of the liars.

**c2** (26:187): They told Shu'ayb to make a piece of the sky fall on them if he was truthful.

**c3** (26:188): Shu'ayb said that his Lord knew best what they did.

**c4** (26:189): They denied him, and the punishment of the day of the shadow seized them.

**c5** (26:189): The ayah says that it was the punishment of a great day.

**c6** (26:190): The Quran says that in this there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers.

**c7** (15:78-79): Another passage says that the Companions of the Thicket were wrongdoers and that God took vengeance on them.

**c8** (38:13): A list of peoples names the Companions of the Thicket, with Thamud and the people of Lut, as the factions.

### One-minute summary

The Companions of the Thicket called Shu'ayb a liar and told him to make a piece of the sky fall on them [c1][c2]. They denied him, and the punishment of the day of the shadow seized them [c4].

### Complete story

They told Shu'ayb that he was one of the bewitched, a human like them, and that they thought him one of the liars [c1]. They told Shu'ayb to make a piece of the sky fall on them if he was truthful [c2]. Shu'ayb said that his Lord knew best what they did [c3]. They denied him, and the punishment of the day of the shadow seized them [c4]. The ayah says that it was the punishment of a great day [c5]. The Quran says that in this there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers [c6]. Another passage says that the Companions of the Thicket were wrongdoers and that God took vengeance on them [c7]. A list of peoples names the Companions of the Thicket, with Thamud and the people of Lut, as the factions [c8].

### Deep study

- They told Shu'ayb that he was one of the bewitched, a human like them, and that they thought him one of the liars (26:177, 26:185-186) [c1].
- They told Shu'ayb to make a piece of the sky fall on them if he was truthful (26:187) [c2].
- Shu'ayb said that his Lord knew best what they did (26:188) [c3].
- They denied him, and the punishment of the day of the shadow seized them (26:189) [c4].
- The ayah says that it was the punishment of a great day (26:189) [c5].
- The Quran says that in this there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers (26:190) [c6].
- Another passage says that the Companions of the Thicket were wrongdoers and that God took vengeance on them (15:78-79) [c7].
- A list of peoples names the Companions of the Thicket, with Thamud and the people of Lut, as the factions (38:13) [c8].

### Kids mode

The Companions of the Thicket did not believe Shu'ayb [c1]. They denied him, and the punishment of the day of the shadow came [c4]. The Quran says that this is a sign [c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayat set a challenge to bring down the sky beside Shu'ayb's reply that his Lord knows best [c2][c3]. One reading is that the reply leaves the judgement with God [c3][c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what the day of the shadow was, or what is meant by the shadow; the ayah gives only the name.
- Not established: 15:79 ends with a dual pronoun whose referents are not named in the ayah; the draft does not use that part.
- Not established: whether the factions of 38:13 are the same peoples as the Companions of the Thicket; the draft states only that the list names them.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any link between the Companions of the Thicket and Madyan, and any date for the event.
